answer: An agent marketplace requires each bidding identity to lock $100 in collateral for 30 days before accepting work. Whether agents sell dune mapping, falcon tracking, or karst surveying, each identity needs its own deposit, and collateral cannot back two identities at once. An attacker running 10,000 fake agents must therefore immobilize $1 million for a month, making a swarm costly even when generating names and keys is free.
